relevance_note: Single-patient case report of SSADHD: "Diagnostic evaluation supported SSADHD, including elevated urinary 4‐hydroxybutyric acid, characteristic MRI abnormalities of the globi pallidi and dentate nuclei, and a homozygous ALDH5A1 missense variant".
method_note: Read only the paper, the schema and the rules. No script was used to transcribe anything; all spans were copied by hand from the Markdown and checked with search. One in-scope person: the single patient of the case report, labelled 'patient' (rule 5; 'the patient'/'our patient' are role words, not labels). The relatives mentioned only in the family history ("an intellectual disability in a maternal relative, and psychotic illness in paternal relatives") were given no rows: the paper gives no individual-level fact and no relation to the in-scope person beyond family history. Table 1 is a hospital-day timeline and Tables 2-3 are medication/diagnostic summaries, not per-patient tables, so they generate no further people; no stacked ' / ' cells occur anywhere in this paper. Catatonia was considered but explicitly not favoured ("Catatonia was therefore retained in the differential diagnosis but was not favored as the primary explanation"), so no catatonia row was emitted. Normal or negative findings were recorded as the abnormality they rule out and marked excluded (afebrile -> fever; urinalysis negative -> urinary tract infection). "No electrographic seizures were recorded" was not used to exclude the broader checklist item 'seizures or epilepsy'. Checklist item 'depression or mood fluctuation' was marked observed on the strength of the printed "affective lability"; this mapping is my judgement. Checklist items never mentioned (hypotonia, motor deficits, ataxia, dystonia, exertional dyskinesia, hemiballismus, autism spectrum disorder, obsessive-compulsive traits, cerebral or cerebellar atrophy) are 'not reported', as is the absence of a per-patient age at diagnosis, parental testing or ethnicity.

vital_status.span: At a more recent follow‐up, she remained connected with psychiatry and primary care and was reported to be doing well with as‐needed olanzapine.

treatment_summary.value: Melatonin used for sleep; bowel regimen continued; hydroxyzine was discontinued because of limited efficacy and concern for anticholinergic burden; quetiapine started; improved sleep, appetite, oral intake, and behavioral regulation; later reported doing well with as-needed olanzapine.

disease_label_as_stated.span: Succinic semialdehyde dehydrogenase deficiency (SSADHD) is a rare inherited neurometabolic disorder caused by deficiency of succinic semialdehyde dehydrogenase, the enzyme encoded by the ALDH5A1 gene

clinical_diagnosis_basis.value: combined biochemical, imaging, clinical, and molecular evidence
span: Molecular testing identified a homozygous ALDH5A1 missense variant, NM_001080.3:c.434A >G (p.Glu145Gly), which was classified as a variant of uncertain significance.
The diagnosis therefore rested on combined biochemical, imaging, clinical, and molecular evidence rather than molecular classification alone
